chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Bilal said:

I wrote to him regarding the time of the Night Prayer, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'At the disappearance of the night, which is its midpoint, is best. If it is missed, then its beginning and its end are permissible.'
ai.seo_question: What is the best time to perform the Night Prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the temporal hierarchy for Salat al-Layl, designating the midpoint of the night as the most virtuous moment for devotion. He further establishes legal flexibility, permitting the prayer at either the beginning or end of the night if the optimal time is missed, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of balancing spiritual excellence with practical accessibility for the believer.
